thread:
ana: Quick thought — we need an operational policy for environment-based TTL + fast rehydrate for prod traces. Current hot/cold split is fine for cost, but during incidents we need sub-minute access to traces. Any objections to a 7d hot window for prod + on-demand rehydrate API with SLA?
will: Sounds reasonable. What's the expected cost if we allow 'rehydrate' to pull from cold storage on-demand? :thinking_face:
dinesh: Doing 7d hot for prod and 24h for staging aligns with current incident cadence. Rehydrate cost depends on how we implement it (full object copy vs streaming). If we stream KV across, it might be cheaper.
kevin: We should also define a prioritization queue for rehydrate requests — incidents > paged > dev. Otherwise paged noise will drown out SRE requests.
sasha: +1 on queue. Also: need dashboard and alerting changes so paging shows whether traces are in hot/cold and rehydrate ETA. Otherwise paging team will be blind.
nana: typo — meant "ana" above not "nana" :)
infra-bot: Note: perf-runner job 2026-06-02T11:23 created a snapshot of trace access patterns (samples stored at s3://redwood-inference/trace-samples/).
nana: fixed :sweat_smile:
nana: proposal sketch: 
```
trace_retention:
  prod: {hot: 7d, cold: 365d}
  staging: {hot: 1d, cold: 90d}
  dev: {hot: 6h, cold: 30d}
rehydrate:
  SLA: {incident: 30s, page: 2m, manual: 30m}
  max_parallel_incident_jobs: 10
  cost_cap_per_day: $200
```
will: That looks strict on SLA (30s) — can we realistically stream and index enough data in 30s? Cold blobs are compressed and chunked. 30s is tight unless we prefetch indexes.
dinesh: Agree. We should separate index fetch vs payload fetch. If we keep trace indices in hot (e.g., last 90d) then pointer-based streaming for payloads might be <30s. Storing a tiny trace index in hot is cheap.
kevin: Index-in-hot is a good compromise. Schema change required though — add compact index objects per trace that live in the hot tier. We can store them in ClickHouse (small rows) and reference S3 blobs.
sasha: UX ask: Console should show "rehydrate progress" with ETA + estimated cost before approving manual rehydrate. Prod incidents should bypass approval if requester is in oncall group.
nana: also want a rate-limit on rehydrate requests to protect cold storage IO. We should enforce per-tenant daily bytes cap in the queue.
infra-bot: perf-runner summary: average rehydrate bytes per trace = 120KB, median latency to stream from cold (current infra) = 8s for 1MB, but we need to test for bursting 50 concurrent rehydrates.
kevin: For implementation plan: 1) add compact index objects to hot (ClickHouse), 2) rehydrate service streams from S3 using pre-signed chunked responses, 3) prioritization queue + quotas, 4) console + alerting. Estimate 3 sprints.
will: Can we prototype with a feature flag that only enables rehydrate for a single team first? We'll need telemetry (OTel spans) instrumenting rehydrate flow.
dinesh: I'll add OTLP spans with tags: rehydrate.requester, priority, estimated_bytes, bytes_streamed. Also record cold->hot promotion events.
sasha: Dashboard work — add a "rehydrate" panel to paging runbook; show current queue depth, avg ETA, and cost burn rate. cc @kevin for the DB schema and @dinesh for spans.
nana: FYI: cost estimate based on perf-runner and S3 egress is ~ $0.0003 per rehydrate-trace; with 1000 traces/day at peak = $0.3/day plus CPU. So the $200/day cap is very conservative but ok for safety.
kevin: Action items: kevin -> RFC for compact index schema + migration plan. dinesh -> OTLP span spec and example instrumentations. sasha -> Console mockups for rehydrate UX and approve-exceptions. ana -> finalize retention numbers and rollout policy.
nana: timeline?
kevin: target MVP behind flag in 3 sprints, pilot with SRE team.
sasha: I'll start mocks this week.
will: I'll prep a short runbook stub for paging.
nana: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: rehydrate-api-prototype feature-flag=on -> staging (build #8142).
nana: leaving this thread to actions, will follow up in the RFC PR.
